hook.text: An employee claims a back injury at work. Security cameras show they were injured playing basketball.

buildup.text: Workers' comp fraud includes faking workplace injuries and claiming non-work injuries happened on the job.

discovery.text: Employers also commit fraud — misclassifying workers to pay lower premiums.

twist.text: Employer fraud actually costs more than employee fraud, but gets far less attention.

climax.text: Workers' comp fraud costs over $30 billion yearly, raising costs for employers and employees alike.

punchline.text: The injury happened. Just not where the claim says.

quiz.question: Who commits more costly workers' compensation fraud?
